account: In 2021 the Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute at Mingyue Lake received requests from clinicians at several large hospitals for a prosthetic arm that patients could move by intention. Xie Haiqiong, the institute's director, says that researchers devised a scheme. It detects and identifies electrical signals at suitable muscle sites and processes them by algorithmic analysis. The scheme lets the user control the hand by intention, without passive motion. Fiscal funds arriving since 2023 under the district's grant-to-equity model supported the project. The institute formed a company to incubate the exoskeleton project. A Guangming Daily feature of 13 August 2024 on Chongqing's Liangjiang New Area opens with Wang Bing (Guangming Daily via Haiwainet and NetEase). He lost both hands in an accident a few years earlier, leaving half of each forearm. He says that he now uses the “smart hand” to eat with a spoon, drink from a cup, shake hands and rotate his wrist. He manages daily life alone and can grip a pen and write his name. The feature writes his name as 王炳. The fitting date is not given.

ai_role.statement: The only description of the technology is institute director Xie Haiqiong's, as quoted by Guangming Daily. It is a scheme that detects and identifies electrical signals at suitable muscle sites and processes them by algorithmic analysis. That lets the user control the hand by intention. No source names a machine-learning method, model, training procedure or accuracy figure. The Monitor's “AI-driven” label rests on that description. The functional gains are Wang Bing's own account in a newspaper feature about the district's commercialization policy. No clinician or independent evaluation is cited.

fields.title: Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute's muscle-signal “smart hand” lets bilateral amputee Wang Bing eat, drink, shake hands and write his name

fields.account: In 2021 the Chongqing Bio-Intelligent Manufacturing Research Institute at Mingyue Lake received requests from clinicians at several large hospitals for a prosthetic arm that patients could move by intention. Xie Haiqiong, the institute's director, says that researchers devised a scheme. It detects and identifies electrical signals at suitable muscle sites and processes them by algorithmic analysis. The scheme lets the user control the hand by intention, without passive motion. Fiscal funds arriving since 2023 under the district's grant-to-equity model supported the project. The institute formed a company to incubate the exoskeleton project. A Guangming Daily feature of 13 August 2024 on Chongqing's Liangjiang New Area opens with Wang Bing (Guangming Daily via Haiwainet and NetEase). He lost both hands in an accident a few years earlier, leaving half of each forearm. He says that he now uses the “smart hand” to eat with a spoon, drink from a cup, shake hands and rotate his wrist. He manages daily life alone and can grip a pen and write his name. The feature writes his name as 王炳. The fitting date is not given.

purpose: Built to let a person with amputated hands control a prosthetic hand through muscle signals. The daily-task function that Wang Bing describes is that purpose. The feature frames the project as an example of the district's policy for commercializing research.

ratings.reason: Per Guangming Daily, Wang Bing, who lost both hands, says he eats with a spoon, drinks from a cup, shakes hands and rotates his wrist. He writes his name and manages daily life alone with the device. A capability restored, reported in his words without clinical assessment.
